scope_boundary: This chapter covers the Preamble to the Indian Constitution, including its text, ingredients (source of authority, nature of state, objectives, date of adoption), detailed explanation of key words (Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic, Republic, Justice, Liberty, Equality, Fraternity), its significance as expressed by constitutional authorities, the judicial controversy over whether it is part of the Constitution (Berubari Union, Kesavananda Bharati, LIC of India), and its amendability under Article 368. The 42nd Amendment (1976) is addressed; other parts of the Constitution are discussed only insofar as they relate to the Preamble. Foreign constitutions are referenced only as comparative examples, not analysed in depth.

natural_clusters.label: Preamble as Part of the Constitution and Amendability
members: Berubari Union case (1960) - not part of Constitution
Kesavananda Bharati case (1973) - part of Constitution, amendable subject to basic features
LIC of India case (1995) - integral part
42nd Amendment (1976) - addition of Socialist, Secular, Integrity
Not a source or prohibition of legislative power
